name: Treaty with the Sauk and Foxes, etc., 1861
aka: Great Nemaha Agency treaty of March 6, 1861
nations: Sac and Fox of the Missouri (Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska)
Báxoje (Iowa): Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska, Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma
promises: Articles 1 and 2: the Sac and Fox reserve of about 32,098 acres would be surveyed and sold at auction for no less than $1.25 an acre, and after expenses half the proceeds held in trust for the Sac and Fox at five percent interest.

Article 3: the Iowa ceded the part of their reserve west of Noheart's Creek as a permanent home for the Sac and Fox, in return for the other half of the net sale proceeds held in trust at five percent; the rest of the Iowa land stayed their exclusive reserve.
Article 5: $1,000 for a schoolhouse and teacher's house for the Sac and Fox and $200 a year for schooling, and $300 a year for Iowa schooling, while the President thought it advisable.
Article 7: no outsider could go on the reservations without a licence from the agent.

breaches.what: On an accounting, the Commission found and entered final judgment that the United States was liable to the Iowa for $2,000.08, the difference between the proceeds of the land sold under this treaty and the amount the Iowa actually received, with interest from October 1, 1871, a total of $10,807.01. The facts were stipulated at a 1965 hearing.

openQuestions: The liability rests on facts the parties stipulated in 1965; the Commission entered it as a finding and final judgment. Jordan may want to decide whether that counts as a Commission finding (it is treated as one here).
Whether the Sac and Fox of the Missouri were paid their half of the sale proceeds in full was not traced; no Sac and Fox decision on this treaty was found in the collection.
Whether the Article 5 school money was spent was not researched.
No Iowa or Sac and Fox history page about this treaty was opened in this pass.
